title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - BioReach
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week POC focused on private networking (VPC peering / PrivateLink) and data residency constraints. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost targets), benchmark plan, region requirements (eu-west-1 primary), egress rules, and next steps to exchange security docs and schedule network testing window.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (BioReach CTO), Rajiv Menon (Head of Infra), Sophie Carter (Security), Tom Alvarez (ML Lead)

Summary (auto):
Brief—confirming POC scope: private networking, data residency, benchmarks and timeline. Identify blockers (proxy, egress, KMS).

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jasmine from Redwood, and Marcus our SE is here to run through the networking details for the POC. Quick roll call?
[00:18] Lena: Hi, Lena here.
[00:20] Rajiv: Rajiv, infra.
[00:23] Sophie: Sophie from security.
[00:25] Tom: Tom, ML.
[00:27] Marcus: Great. Quick agenda—network connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region and data residency constraints, egress restrictions, and then benchmark/success criteria.
[00:40] Lena: Our legal and security teams need data to remain in EU, ideally eu-west-1. We have strict egress rules and everything must go over the corporate proxy unless we can do private peering.
[00:54] Marcus: Understood. We commonly offer three patterns: hosted over TLS (internet), VPC peering, or AWS PrivateLink. For eu-west-1 we can stand up endpoints in the region. VPC peering gives you full network access to the Redwood nodes, PrivateLink is a managed endpoint model and tends to be simpler for strict egress.
[01:12] Rajiv: Can you explain the tradeoffs again? We prefer not to add public egress from our subnets.
[01:20] Marcus: Sure—VPC peering is a one-time peering relationship, low latency, but it requires route table changes and we need to coordinate CIDR overlaps. PrivateLink (AWS) gives you ENIs and an endpoint service; egress stays within AWS backbone. It also avoids asymmetric routing. Peering is good if you want to reach other services in our VPC, PrivateLink is more locked down.
[01:45] Sophie: From security, we prefer minimized attack surface; PrivateLink sounds better. But we need to validate certs, mutual TLS, and KMS key policies for encryption at rest.
[01:56] Marcus: We support TLS with mutual auth for PrivateLink. For encryption at rest, customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed KMS options exist; for Private deployment we can integrate with your KMS/HSM via IAM roles and encrypted tunnels—we'll share the exact KMS integration doc.
[02:20] Jasmine: Important to call out: for the POC we can run in eu-west-1 with PrivateLink; if BioReach needs a fully private control plane we have a Private deployment option but that adds time. POC will focus on inference endpoints only.
[02:35] Tom: Quick question on model weights: do they leave the region?
[02:39] Marcus: No. In the PrivateLink and dedicated region setup, model execution stays in the region. We don't replicate to other regions unless you enable cross-region failover.
[02:49] Lena: Good. On egress we have a forward proxy for outbound traffic; can Redwood work with that?
[02:55] Marcus: Yes, but proxying adds latency. For benchmarking we prefer direct PrivateLink peering so we measure baseline performance. If you must proxy, we'll measure that path too.
[03:12] Rajiv: What IPs do we need to whitelist?
[03:15] Jasmine: We'll provide a small block of egress IPs. For PrivateLink you typically don't need to whitelist, but you need to allow the ENI traffic. We'll send exact CIDRs and port list.
[03:30] Sophie: Compliance — SOC2 and audit logs. Can Redwood provide audit logs for inference requests and token usage?
[03:38] Jasmine: Yes, we emit per-request logs to your destination (S3 or remote syslog) with redaction options. We'll include that in the docs.
[03:45] Marcus: Also point: KV cache and batching behavior—we'll document how we handle prefix caching in case you have PII concerns and how to disable caching for sensitive prompts.
[03:58] Tom: Benchmarks — what do you need from us?
[04:02] Marcus: We'll need sample prompt sets (1k prompts), typical sequence lengths (avg/95th), and target QPS. For the POC success criteria propose: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms for 512-token context for single-stream inference; throughput target 20 req/sec sustained; correctness/quality checks via a small eval set. Those are negotiable.
[04:30] Tom: 20 req/sec sounds reasonable for our test banner. We care more about p95 than p50.
[04:36] Lena: Cost target? We have budget constraints.
[04:38] Jasmine: We'll provide estimated per-token and per-request costs for hosted vs dedicated. POC will include a cost model run for your workload.
[04:47] Rajiv: Timeline — how long to get networking set up?
[04:50] Marcus: For PrivateLink typically 2-3 days to exchange certs and configure endpoints once we have IAM and CIDRs. VPC peering can be similar but needs route table confirmation. Full POC is 3–4 weeks: week 1 connectivity, week 2 baseline benchmarks, week 3 tuning & security checks, week 4 evaluation and report.
[05:12] Sophie: Are there any common gotchas?
[05:15] Marcus: Overlapping CIDRs, proxy timeouts, MTU issues with ENIs, and egress inspection appliances that break TLS. We'll share a checklist to mitigate these.
[05:25] Jasmine: We'll also run a small smoke test once network is up — simple echo requests and a 100-request perf run.
[05:33] Rajiv: For the benchmark scripts, what do you run?
[05:36] Marcus: We use k6 and a custom driver that simulates token streaming and records p50/p95 and tokens/sec. We'll share the script and the exact payloads.
[05:45] Tom: On data retention, what logs persist on Redwood side?
[05:49] Jasmine: By default we retain request metadata and aggregated cost metrics for 30 days; for PII we can disable request logging or redact content. For enterprise we can set retention windows or forward logs to your S3/Kinesis.
[06:05] Sophie: We need that in writing.
[06:07] Jasmine: We'll include retention and redaction options in the security pack.
[06:12] Marcus: One more note — if you route through your proxy the p95 will likely jump due to idle connection timeouts; we recommend PrivateLink for POC accuracy.
[06:25] Rajiv: OK. About benchmarks — do you support streaming responses for LL generation?
[06:28] Marcus: Yes, we support streaming with chunked transfer. We'll measure both streaming and non-streaming performance. For streaming p95 is measured for first token and steady-state throughput.
[06:40] Lena: For region failover planning, if eu-west-1 goes down what's the process?
[06:44] Jasmine: We can configure fallback to a second region but that may violate your residency policy. For POC we'll not enable cross-region failover unless you permit it.
[06:55] Tom: Any additional security integrations? SSO, RBAC?
[06:58] Jasmine: We support SAML SSO for the console and per-route RBAC. We'll pass the admin docs.
[07:06] Sophie: Also need encryption in transit assurance and a pen-test schedule.
[07:10] Marcus: We'll include TLS cert details and penetration testing guidance; we can coordinate timelines.
[07:20] Jasmine: Ok to recap next steps?
[07:23] Lena: Yes.
[07:24] Jasmine: Redwood will: 1) send private networking checklist, endpoint IPs/CIDRs and Terraform snippet; 2) Marcus will share benchmark plan and scripts; 3) security pack with SOC2, retention, KMS options. BioReach will: 1) confirm region eu-west-1 and whitelist capabilities, 2) provide sample prompts and sequence length stats, 3) schedule 2-hour window on 2026-06-16 for connectivity test.
[07:53] Rajiv: We'll confirm firewall rules and send the proxy config by Friday.
[07:58] Sophie: We'll also compile a list of compliance Qs and send.
[08:02] Jasmine: Great. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the connectivity test and a shared doc.
[08:08] Tom: One last thing — can you run a small quality eval vs our current in-house model?
[08:12] Marcus: Yes, we can run side-by-side evals as part of the POC; add that to the benchmark plan.
[08:18] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[08:20] Jasmine: Thanks all, we'll send the pack by Monday morning.

End of call.
